newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Peso fall drives Manila grains buyers to sidelines.
newsitem.headline: Peso fall drives Manila grains buyers to sidelines.

text.p: MANILA, July 14 - Philippine grains importers would generally ignore the market this week as a result of a sharp fall in the peso but they could buy U.S. soft wheat since it was trading at low levels, Manila grains traders said on Monday.
"It's difficult to rush into this market. You might meet a disaster," said a senior Manila trader.

Most Philippine wheat importers shelved import plans on Friday after the peso plunged 11.5 percent to 29.45 after the central bank said it was allowing the peso to trade in a wider band, which effectively meant a devaluation of the currency.

But an executive at a local flour miller said while most Philippine firms stayed away from the market, scared that a devalued peso would bloat their import costs, his company bought 18,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for July and August shipment.
U.S. wheat suppliers said they had not heard of any Philippine mill that bought 18,000 tonnes of wheat last week.
"Because import inquiry is low, it is the best time to buy western white wheat after its futures price hit a low in three years last week," the executive said.
Traders said the USDA forecast that U.S. wheat output would reach 2.431 billion bushels, up seven percent from the 1996 level, was within their expectations.
"The USDA forecast has no bearing on us. The market is at a standstill due to the peso volatility," one trader said.
Traders said corn, rice, soymeal and soybean buyers are also expected to shy away from the market due to ample supplies.
The prevailing flour and corn prices in Manila in peso:
Retail price of yellow corn per kg 9.70 9.67
Retail price of white corn per kg 9.47 9.90
